quizName: Hardest Questions in Illinois Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you faster, which increases danger.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like food and drinks. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts to affect you.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol quickly once it is in your system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes and starts to affect you.
questions.explanation: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
It gets the attention of other drivers.
They should make eye contact with nearby drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot.

questions.question: What is usually the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only increase danger by causing them to continue tailgating at a higher speed.

questions.question: In Illinois, are motorcycle safety helmets required?

options.text: Yes, the operator must wear one.
Yes, the passenger must wear one.
Yes, both the operator and passenger must wear one.

questions.explanation: Illinois law does not require motorcycle helmets. However, wearing a properly-fitted helmet is highly recommended.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction. Dry pavement provides the best traction for tires.

questions.question: Which fabric offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, like cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no visible defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects can be stronger than when using either alone.
The effects are less dangerous than using either alone.
The effects usually cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects can be stronger than when using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Some drugs become more dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: Is using both brakes the best way to stop quickly?
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Do most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long. They often occur within the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: When braking, should you only use the rear brake?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When braking, which brake should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when used together.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle completely?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed to find how many drinks remain. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks remaining.
